questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain the preaching of John the Baptist as a preparation for Jesus' ministry.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Luke presents John the Baptist as the forerunner of Jesus. His birth is announced by Gabriel, who says that John will go before the Lord "in the spirit and power of Elijah" to make ready a people prepared for him (1:16-17). John's preaching (3:1-20) prepares the way for Jesus in several ways.

**1. The setting and the prophecy.** Luke dates John's call carefully, in the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar (3:1-2), and quotes Isaiah 40: "Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight" (3:4-6). John is thus the voice in the wilderness whom the prophet had announced, and his work is a preparation for the coming of the Lord.

**2. A call to repentance.** John preaches "a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins" (3:3). Repentance is the first step: people must turn from their old way of life before they can receive the one who is to come. Jesus too later says that he has come to call sinners to repentance (5:32).

**3. A warning against false security.** John tells the crowds that descent from Abraham is not enough: "bear fruits worthy of repentance", for God can raise children to Abraham from stones, and the axe is already at the root of the trees (3:7-9). This removes the idea that membership of the chosen people is a guarantee of salvation and prepares for Jesus' teaching about faith and conduct.

**4. Ethical teaching.** When the crowds ask what they must do, John tells them to share clothing and food, tax collectors to collect no more than is due, and soldiers not to extort money or accuse falsely (3:10-14). The concern for justice and mercy anticipates the social teaching of Jesus.

**5. Pointing to a greater one.** The people wonder whether John might be the Messiah, but John answers that one more powerful is coming, whose sandals he is not worthy to untie, who will baptise "with the Holy Spirit and fire" (3:15-17). He deliberately places himself below Jesus and directs his hearers to him.

**6. Suffering as a forerunner.** John is imprisoned by Herod Antipas after he rebukes him (3:19-20), which anticipates the opposition that Jesus will meet. Luke mentions this before the baptism of Jesus (3:21-22), which marks the point where the ministry of John gives way to that of Jesus.

**Conclusion.** John's preaching prepares for Jesus by announcing the coming of the Lord, calling for repentance and a changed life, warning against false confidence, and pointing to a greater one. His message creates a repentant and expectant people to whom Jesus' own ministry will be addressed.
